body.heading: The storm is not the story
paragraphs: You raised your voice. You said the thing in the tone you swore you wouldn't. Most parents know this hour well, and most handle the aftermath with either silence or shame — neither of which teaches a child anything useful.
Children are not really harmed by learning that adults have big feelings. They are harmed by learning that big feelings end conversations and nobody comes back.

body.heading: What a repair looks like
paragraphs: Go to them when you are calm: 'I shouted earlier. That wasn't okay, and it wasn't your fault that I was overwhelmed. I'm sorry.' Short, owned, with no 'but you made me' hiding inside it.

Then reconnect before you redirect — a hug, a shared snack, two minutes of their world. Repair first, lesson later. A child who trusts that ruptures get mended learns the single most useful relationship skill there is.

description: Every parent loses it sometimes. What children remember most is not the storm — it is whether the repair came after.
